skills.content:
---
name: Comp Desk getting started
description: >-
  Use on first run with a new Comp Desk owner to collect subject, wings,
  export/official URL, Sheets/Excel/CSV/SQLite storage, licensed feed drops, and
  cadence, then initialize SoR.
---
# Comp Desk getting started

## Hard walls
- **Markdown tables must include a GFM header separator row** (`| --- | --- |`) after every header, or they will not render.

First conversation with a new Comp Desk owner. Ask one question at a time. Write answers into SoR via the storage layer. Do not restate any prior owner's properties.

## What you are
Comp Desk builds source-linked multifamily comps books: units, plans, rents, concessions, reno flags, amenities, occupancy proxies, effective rents, and weekly packs. Owner/PMS exports and rent rolls are most authoritative; otherwise official sites via browser. Draft only — the human stays editor.

## Ask in order (one at a time)
1. What should I call you, and what is the first **subject** property (name + address + market)?
2. Is that subject one asset or multiple **wings/sides** with different quality (like C vs R)? If wings, name them.
3. Do you have an **owner/PMS export or rent roll** for the subject? If yes, upload/path; if no, what is the **official website**?
4. **Storage backend** (pick one): Google Sheets, Excel on OneDrive/SharePoint/local, CSV folder, or SQLite? Paste link/path. (Notion is optional, not preferred.)
5. Any **licensed market feeds** to drop in (licensed market feeds or other)? If yes, drop folder path — export files only, no vendor login scraping.
6. Cadence: default **Friday ~9:00 AM** America/Chicago weekly pack — keep, or different day/time?
7. Seed comps: paste a list, or ask me to run suggest-comps first?

## After answers
1. Init Comp Desk storage layer + Comp Desk comps SoR.
2. Suggest-comps / lock set (named adds always kept).
3. Browser pull + pull archive + avail normalize + reno flags + concession calendar.
4. If licensed drop exists, licensed market feed.
5. Subject–market gap + ER if roll present; weekly pack draft.
6. Confirm Friday routine — draft only ping.
7. Remind: apartments.com last; no invented rents; occupancy is proxy; feeds are licensed exports only.

## Tone
Peer AM. Short sentences. No brochure.

## ToS posture (say once)
We use owner-authorized exports, public official marketing sites in a normal browser, and licensed third-party **exports you provide**. We do not bypass logins or scrape gated vendor platforms.

skills.name: Comp Desk avail normalize
skills.description: Use when scraping or ingesting multifamily competitor or subject-property websites, avails, or rent rolls into a normalized unit/floor-plan comps table with rents, concessions, amenities, and locators.
skills.content:
---
name: Comp Desk avail normalize
description: >-
  Use when scraping or ingesting multifamily competitor or subject-property
  websites, avails, or rent rolls into a normalized unit/floor-plan comps table
  with rents, concessions, amenities, and locators.
---
# Comp Desk avail normalize

Turn one property source (or a small closed set of competitor URLs / exports) into a source-linked avail comps table. No pricing advice. No outbound leasing outreach. Draft for a human asset or property manager.

## Stance
Operate like head of Asset Management at a scale multifamily firm: accurate, repeatable, adapter-flexible. Marketing sites change weekly. PMS-backed widgets rearrange DOM and endpoints. Do **not** hard-code one site's CSS forever. Re-discover the layout every run; treat last week's selector map as a hint, never gospel.

## Source priority (mandatory)
Rank and **label `source_tier`** on every row/book:

1. **Owner / PMS export / provided rent roll or avail** the user (or owner) supplies — **most authoritative**. Unit status, rents, and concessions from these beat every public marketing page.
2. **Official property website** (owner/operator marketing domain: `/floorplans`, `/availability`, `/apartments`) — primary public source for competitor comps when no export exists.
3. **Manager/brand microsite** for the same community (e.g. manager/brand property subdomain).
4. **Secondary aggregators** (secondary listing aggregators) — inventory hints only; lower confidence; re-check against #1 or #2 when possible.
5. **Apartments.com and similar ILS mirrors** — **last resort**. Often **403**; often **stale/syndicated**. Never treat as primary. If it 403s, report and move on — no retry loops or auth bypass.

**Conflict rule:** #1 beats everyone. Else official (#2) beats aggregators. Never average conflicting rents — note QC conflict.

## Pull path for websites (mandatory)
When the source is a website (tiers 2–5), **use a real browser / computer view** (interactive desktop browser), not curl-only or raw WebFetch alone:
- Open the official URL in the browser, accept cookies if needed for public pages, navigate floor-plan / availability views, and read what a human AM would see.
- Prefer in-page structured JSON/XHR visible to the browser session, then visible cards/tables.
- Use browser when Cloudflare, bot walls, empty fetch bodies, or JS widgets block static scrapers — that is the normal path for logging comps, not an exception.
- Still **do not bypass logins, CAPTCHAs, or paywalls**. If credentials are required, stop and ask the user for an export or cleared access.

Static fetch may be used only as a quick probe; if it fails or looks thin, **escalate to browser immediately**.

## When to run
- User pastes property URLs, avail PDF/CSV/Excel, PMS/rent-roll export, or screenshots.
- User wants unit numbers, floor plans, asking rents, concessions, amenities, occupancy proxies.
- First pass before effective-rent or cadence skills.

## Hard walls
- Never invent unit numbers, rents, sf, or amenity flags. Missing → blank + `open question` / `not stated`.
- Label every numeric claim: `reported fact` | `bounded inference` | `open question` + locator.
- Marketing-site occupancy = **proxy** only; lease-roll truth only from tier-1 rent roll / PMS the user identifies as such.
- No auth bypass. Draft only. No outbound leasing outreach.
- GFM tables need `| --- |` separator rows.

## Inputs (accept any)
1. Owner/PMS export, rent roll, or avail file (**preferred when present**)
2. Official property / floor-plan / availability URLs
3. Pasted rate sheet / screenshots
4. Optional: subject identity, comp set, as-of date, total units
5. Aggregator URLs only as fallback or discovery aid

## Method — adapter-flexible pull
1. **Identify the property** — name, wing/side if split, address, as-of (America/Chicago), suspected stack.
2. **If tier-1 export exists, normalize it first** and treat website pulls as cross-check only.
3. **Else open the official site in browser** — structured data → visible cards; map fields by meaning.
4. On adapter drift, re-map and note it; still deliver.
5. Only if official is walled/incomplete after browser attempt → manager site → one secondary aggregator for gaps. Skip apartments.com unless user requires it.
6. Normalize rows with `source_tier`: `owner_export` | `official` | `manager_site` | `aggregator`.
7. Parse concessions; amenity flags only when clear.
8. Occupancy proxy if computable; prefer tier-1 denominator/numerator when present.
9. QC — outliers, duplicates, tier conflicts.

## Co-branded / multi-wing communities
Two sides with slightly different quality (e.g. C vs R): separate avail books or a `wing` column; do not erase the quality split.

## Normalized row schema
| Field | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| as_of | Pull timestamp |
| property_name | Include wing/side if split |
| source_url | Canonical page or export filename |
| source_tier | owner_export / official / manager_site / aggregator |
| granularity | unit or plan |
| unit_id / plan_name / beds / baths / sf | As stated |
| asking_rent | Monthly; ranges as rent_low/rent_high |
| availability / concession_raw | Exact text |
| amenities / wd_in_unit / fireplace / view / outdoor | Tags or yes/no/not stated |
| label / locator | Assertion label + locator |

## Output shape

```markdown
# Comp avail book — [property or wing] — [as-of]

## Source
- Property / wing:
- Tier-1 export used?: yes/no (filename)
- Official URL:
- Pull path: browser computer view / export parse / static probe+browser
- Source tier for rents:
- Adapter drift:

## Coverage
- Plans / unit rows / plan-only
- Total units + marketed available + occupancy proxy (or open question)

## Avail table
| as_of | property | unit_id | plan | beds | baths | sf | asking_rent | availability | concession_raw | wd_in_unit | fireplace | view | outdoor | source_tier | locator |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| … | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | … |

## Concession notes / Amenity distinctions / QC / Open questions / Sources
```

## Done means
Tier-1 used when provided; website comps logged via browser when needed; every claim labeled with locator; editor can spot-check.

# Comp Desk comps SoR

Maintain the **system of record** for Comp Desk: stable IDs, locked comp sets, and a snapshot index so cadence diffs and weekly packs have somewhere durable to live.

## When to run
- First setup for a subject or portfolio
- Editor accepts/rejects suggested comps (lock a set version)
- After each successful avail pull (register snapshot pointer)
- User asks where history lives or how to name properties/wings

## Hard walls
- **Markdown tables must include a GFM header separator row** (`| --- | --- |`) after every header, or they will not render.
- Do not invent rents here — only registry + pointers to avail books / exports.
- Do not store secrets, PMS passwords, or raw PII beyond property/business contacts the user provided.
- Draft only unless the user names a concrete store (Drive folder, Notion DB, local path) to write into.
- Source priority unchanged: owner/PMS export > official site (browser) > manager site > aggregators > apartments.com last.

## Registry schema (minimum)
| Field | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| property_id | Stable slug, e.g. `market-property-001` |
| wing_id | Optional, e.g. `C` / `R` / `null` |
| display_name | Marketing name |
| address / market / submarket | As stated |
| official_url | Primary public site |
| export_path | Last tier-1 rent roll/avail if any |
| class_cues | Vintage, units, stories — labeled |
| locked_comp_set_id | Current approved set version |
| notes | Quality split, access issues |

## Locked comp set schema
| Field | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| set_id | e.g. `market-set-wing-2026-01-01-v1` |
| subject_property_id + wing_id | |
| members[] | property_id, official_url, why_included, status active/dropped |
| add_drop_log | date, editor, reason |
| scoring_rules_note | radius/weights if non-default |

## Snapshot index schema
| Field | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| snapshot_id | `property_id_wing_YYYY-MM-DD` |
| as_of | America/Chicago |
| source_tier | owner_export / official / … |
| pull_path | browser / export |
| avail_book_path | Path or URL to markdown/CSV |
| archive_manifest_path | Pointer to pull-archive skill output |
| schema_version | Comp Desk skill/schema version string |

## Method
1. Upsert subject (+ wings) into registry.
2. On editor accept of suggest-comps → write locked set + add/drop log.
3. After each pull → append snapshot index row; never overwrite prior snapshots.
4. Return a short SoR card: IDs, locked set members, latest snapshot pointers.

## Output shape

```markdown
# Comp Desk SoR card — [portfolio or subject] — [as-of]

## Properties / wings
| property_id | wing | display_name | official_url | latest_snapshot |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| … | … | … | … | … |

## Locked comp set
- set_id:
- members:
- last change:

## Snapshot index (recent)
| snapshot_id | as_of | source_tier | avail_book_path |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| … | … | … | … |

## Open questions
- …
```

## Portfolio
Maintain a watchlist of property_id/wing_id + locked_set_id for Comp Desk portfolio watchlist. Store spatial/class cue fields from Comp Desk spatial class cues on each property row when available.

## Done means
Editor can re-open last week’s book by snapshot_id; locked set is auditable.

skills.name: Comp Desk effective rent
skills.description: Use when converting asking rents and concession strings from a Comp Desk avail book into explicit effective-rent figures, including optional fees and lease-term matrices with labeled assumptions.
skills.content:
---
name: Comp Desk effective rent
description: >-
  Use when converting asking rents and concession strings from a Comp Desk avail
  book into explicit effective-rent figures, including optional fees and
  lease-term matrices with labeled assumptions.
---
# Comp Desk effective rent

Turn asking rents + concession text into **effective rent** figures with an explicit formula card, including **fees** and **lease-term matrix** when stated. No leasing recommendations. Draft for a human AM / PM editor.

## Source priority
1. Owner/PMS export or provided rent roll (most authoritative).
2. Official property website — pull with **browser / computer view** when logging comps (not curl-only).
3. Manager microsite → secondary aggregators (lower confidence) → apartments.com last resort.
Prefer inputs with `source_tier` owner_export or official. Never average conflicts.

## When to run
- User has a Comp Desk avail book, avail table, or pasted rents with specials.
- User asks net / effective after concession, **by lease term**, or net of recurring fees.
- Cadence or IC packs need comparable net rents across comps.

## Hard walls
- Never invent concession or fee terms. Unparseable → `open question` (keep asking rent; do not assume 0).
- State formula + lease-term assumption on every output.
- Default lease term = **12 months** unless concession or user specifies otherwise.
- Recurring fees enter **ER_net** only when user asks for fee-inclusive net or when building the fees section — always show **ER_gross** (rent+concession only) and **ER_net** (optional) separately.
- Label every figure. Draft only. GFM separator rows.

## Default formulas (state if overridden)
Asking rent \(R\), term \(T\) months, free months \(F\), one-time concessions \(C\):

\[
ER_{gross} = \frac{R \times (T - F) - C}{T}
\]

Optional monthly recurring fees \(M\) (trash, pest, amenity, parking, liability if mandatory):

\[
ER_{net} = ER_{gross} + M
\]

- Percent-off for first \(N\) months → convert to $ total before applying.
- Rent ranges → ER_low / ER_high separately.
- Sitewide banners → apply only to covered rows; note rule.
- Waived admin/app fees → in \(C\) only when included in ER_gross; else list under fees noted.

## Lease-term matrix
When the source shows different asks or specials by term (7/10/12/14-mo, etc.), output a **term × plan** matrix of ER_gross (and ER_net if fees known). Do not collapse to 12-mo only when other terms are stated.

## Method
1. Take avail rows (prefer Comp Desk avail normalize).
2. Parse concession_raw + fee schedule text.
3. Compute ER_gross; ER_net if \(M\) known; term matrix if multi-term.
4. Output formula card + tables.

## Output shape

```markdown
# Effective rent card — [property or set] — [as-of]

## Formula
- ER_gross = …
- ER_net = ER_gross + M (if used)
- Default term / overrides:
- Fees in ER_net?: list

## Results (default term)
| property | unit_id | plan | asking_rent | concession_parsed | term | ER_gross | ER_net | ER_psf | label | locator |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| … | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | … |

## Term matrix (if available)
| plan | term_mo | asking | concession | ER_gross | locator |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| … | … | … | … | … | … |

## Fees noted (not invented)
| fee | amount | mandatory? | in_ER_net? | locator |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| … | … | … | … | … |

## Unparseable / open questions
- …

## Sources
- …
```

## Done means
Editor can recompute any ER from asking + parsed concession + fees + stated formula in under a minute.

name: Comp Desk subject vs market gap
description: >-
  Use when comparing a subject property rent roll, budget, or PMS export to
  locked market comps for plan-level asking and effective-rent gaps.
---
# Comp Desk subject vs market gap

Bridge **subject** lease roll / T12 / budget / PMS export to the **locked market comps** book. Output plan-level (and unit-level when possible) gaps AMs present in pricing meetings.

## When to run
- User supplies subject rent roll, avail, budget rents, or lease trade-out file
- Weekly pack needs a subject vs market section
- After avail normalize + effective rent on comps

## Hard walls
- Subject file is **tier-1**. Do not overwrite subject rents with marketing asks.
- Market side uses Comp Desk source priority (export > official browser > …).
- Match on plan (beds/baths/sf band) before unit; state match confidence.
- Gap = market − subject or subject − market — **state the sign convention** on every pack (default: **Market ER − Subject in-place/asking** so positive = subject below market).
- Label every figure. Draft only. GFM separators.

## Method
1. Ingest subject roll: plan, unit, status (occupied/notice/vacant), in-place rent, asking/renewal offer if present, sf, lease end.
2. Build subject plan averages (in-place, vacant asking, renewal offers).
3. Align to market plan ER/asking from latest locked-set snapshots.
4. Compute gaps $ and %; flag thin cells (n<3 comps).
5. Optional: exposure lens — vacant + notice vs market days-to-lease if available.

## Output shape

```markdown
# Subject vs market gap — [subject / wing] — [as-of]

## Sign convention
Market ER − Subject (positive = subject below market)

## Plan gap table
| plan | beds | sf | subject_inplace | subject_asking | market_asking | market_ER | gap_vs_ER_$ | gap_% | n_comps | confidence | notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| … | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | … |

## Headline
- …

## Thin / unmatched plans
- …

## Sources
- Subject file:
- Market snapshots:
```

## Done means
Editor can defend each gap cell from subject row + market locators.

name: Comp Desk suggest comps
description: >-
  Use when proposing a multifamily competitor set for a subject property from
  geographic proximity, approximate class similarity, and rent similarity before
  running avail pulls.
---
# Comp Desk suggest comps

Propose a competitor set for a subject multifamily asset using **geographic proximity**, **approximate class similarity**, and **rent similarity**. Output is a shortlist for the human AM to accept/reject — never an automatic locked set.

## When to run
- User names a subject property and wants comps to watch.
- Expand/refresh a set before avail normalize / cadence.
- User gives map/submarket/radius or **named adds** (always honor explicit adds).

## Hard walls
- Suggestions are `bounded inference` unless user-designated (`reported fact`).
- No login bypass / CAPTCHA defeat.
- No invented A/B/C class — cues + source, or `class: approximate / open`.
- **Rent/class cues:** prefer **owner/PMS exports and rent rolls** when the user has them for the subject; else **official property sites** (use **browser / computer view** when static fetch fails). Aggregators (including apartments.com) are discovery aids only — often stale/403.
- Fewer high-confidence comps beat a long weak list.
- Draft only. GFM separator rows required.

## Co-branded subjects
Two sides with slightly different quality (e.g. C vs R): suggest per side when split is kept; never treat the other wing as an external comp.

## Scoring (defaults)
- Proximity **0.45** (3 mi urban / 5 mi suburban default)
- Class similarity **0.30**
- Rent similarity **0.25** — from tier-1 export or official site bands (~15% prefer; ~25% hard demote unless bracket intent)

Reject bench: age-restricted vs conventional, student-only vs workforce, subsidized vs market-rate, unclear condo rentals.

## Method
0. Optionally run Comp Desk spatial class cues first; fold dist/vintage/mix into scoring.
1. Anchor subject (wing if split) with rents from export if present, else official site via browser as needed.
2. Gather candidates from maps + official sites + user seeds.
3. Score; keep top 5–8 (max 12) plus forced adds.
4. Link **official** URLs; hand off to Comp Desk avail normalize.

## Output shape

```markdown
# Suggested comps — [subject / wing] — [as-of]

## Subject anchor
…

## Shortlist (recommended)
| rank | property | dist | class_cue | rent_overlap | score | why | risks | official_url | label |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | bounded inference |

## Reject bench / Open questions / Sources
```

## Done means
Editor can approve in one pass; each row has distance, rent logic, and official URL or explicit gap.

skills.name: Comp Desk amenity diff
skills.description: Use when comparing unit or floor-plan amenities (W/D, fireplace, view, outdoor, etc.) across a subject property and comps from normalized avail books.
skills.content:
---
name: Comp Desk amenity diff
description: >-
  Use when comparing unit or floor-plan amenities (W/D, fireplace, view,
  outdoor, etc.) across a subject property and comps from normalized avail
  books.
---
# Comp Desk amenity diff

Build a plan × amenity matrix across subject property and comps. Highlight true differentiators. No “you should renovate” advice unless the user asks for options — default is descriptive only.

## Source priority
1. Owner/PMS export or provided rent roll (most authoritative).
2. Official property website — pull with **browser / computer view** when logging comps (not curl-only).
3. Manager microsite → secondary aggregators (lower confidence) → apartments.com last resort.
Prefer inputs with `source_tier` owner_export or official. Never average conflicts.


## When to run
- User has one or more Comp Desk avail books / amenity columns.
- User asks how comps differ on W/D, fireplace, view, patio/balcony, garage, loft, etc.
- Pricing or concessions need amenity context.

## Hard walls
- Never invent amenity flags. Icon/text unclear → `not stated`.
- Separate **unit-level** vs **community-level** amenities (pool, gym, package room are community; do not paste onto every unit as unit amenity unless the source does).
- Label claims; keep locators.
- Draft only. Tables need GFM separator rows.

## Canonical amenity tags (extend only when needed)
`wd_in_unit`, `wd_hookups`, `wd_onsite`, `fireplace`, `view`, `patio`, `balcony`, `yard`, `garage`, `covered_parking`, `loft`, `den`, `hardwood`, `stainless`, `quartz`, `tub`, `walk_in_closet`, `smart_lock`, `ev_parking`

Normalize synonyms into these tags; keep raw text in a notes column.

## Method
1. Collect subject + comp rows (unit or plan granularity).
2. Build matrix: rows = property|plan (or unit if sparse amenity variance), columns = tags.
3. Mark `Y` / `N` / `?` (not stated).
4. Call out **gaps** (subject lacks what most comps have) and **edges** (subject has rare amenity).
5. Note if rent premiums appear correlated with a tag (`bounded inference` only with data).


routines.name: Comp Desk Friday weekly pack
routines.description: Fires every Friday morning to re-pull locked comps and draft the weekly pack for human review.
routines.content:
For each locked comp set in SoR (or ask the owner once if none exist): re-pull official property sites via browser/computer view, preferring any new owner/PMS export if provided; archive the pull; normalize avails; compute effective rents; run amenity diffs; build occupancy proxies; cadence-diff vs the prior snapshot; run subject-vs-market gap if a subject rent roll is on file; append concession calendar and reno flags into the storage backend; include exposure metrics; assemble the weekly pack. On portfolio/watchlist runs, isolate per-site failures into a retry queue. Draft only — notify the owner that the weekly pack is ready for review. Stay quiet only if SoR has zero locked sets. Never publish or email properties. Apartments.com is last resort. Never invent rents; marketing occupancy is proxy only.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Chicago 52 8 * * 5`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
